Lovely game, the style is amazing, the exploration aspect of the game just amazes me. Encountering the infinite for the very first time just makes the experience and the money spent worth it in my opinion. Although Astronner has a lot of pros (which may not be mentioned here) it also has some cons, for example the multiplayer can be kind of wonky at times, some minor bugs like walking on air and such. Overall Astroneer is a very fun game to play and in my opinion is worth every penny.

There is one question you should ask yourself before buying this awesome game, do I like space? If no than you will probably not like this game and I'm just wasting your time. If yes, you might want to get it because it is absoloute cinema and is fun.

It's a great space-themed sandbox that tries to be more chill and relaxing with zero combat and its focus more on base building and resource gathering. It's a refreshing change so I come back for a playthrough once every year. My main issue is the limited inventory, especially in the late game. 10 slots is simply NOT enough (solvable through modding). Some people complain about the amount of grinding but it was never an issue for me, especially since resource gathering can be automated.

Loading properties absolutely suck in this game. Don't park vehicles on uneven surfaces or you risk losing it all by being flung into space. If you do plan on making Big Rover give it a trailer this does seem to slightly help the physics collisions. Also play with friends, this game would be quite boring alone and the teamwork is nice.

the only problem: the only problem is a double edged sword as its a good gameplay loop yet it makes me not like exploring new planets
every time you are in a new planet you have to set up a mininum base for each planet and its quite a pain but it really does make the experience worse and better and i have no idea to fix this problem.

it has such a gorgeous style. I think personally that it gets boring somewhat fast, its easy to run out of things to do. Theres really not much threat, even on the "super dangerous" planets. But its super relaxing and just gorgeous, looks great and plays smoothly, even with high ping. Does get a little laggy after a bit if you have too many tethers or people are far apart but its nothing you cant deal with

Astroneer. Simple fun, no questions about it. Get you a group of friends and just have at it, this game lends itself to being an extremely casual game and I look forward to further updates, and hopefully more challenges to overcome. If you're looking for a challenge, this game is not the one, it CAN get rather boring, especially if you're not familiar, at least at the time, with everything necessary, but jump into caves, ramp off the mountains, and yank up some hostile plants, and while you're at it experience the silly physics with winches.

The worst of the EULA has been changed. So my original review may not apply.

Astroneer was released too early. This game is full of game-breaking bugs, multiplayer latency and is generally unusable. There were considerably less bugs in the previous, Early Access version.

I would wait on buying this, at least until the major glitches are corrected.

Update December 3rd, 2019: Multiplayer is still a mess.

JUST DO IT! I have been an Astroneer since day one and played this on both steam and Xbox versions, with serveral hundred hours inputted and am still hooked. With it's stunning visuals and adventurous game play this game allows you to play your way, stay on your home planet of terran or blast of to distant worlds to make a new home and find new exciting minerals to use as you progress through the game. What makes this game my favourite is not only the gameplay itself but the highly devoted DEV team behind it, with it now just entering into the Alpha stage its still in development and team SES strives to keep progressing there game and engages the community every step of the way. Watching this game grow from day one release to now has been a fantastic experiance and I look forward to every update which brings this game further and further to a game thats out of this world. Thanks Team SES

The soundtrack and the graphics are mesmerizing. It's really fun gathering resources and preparing for a trip to another planet, or establishing a new bases even tho you don't really need them. I bought this game like 2-3 years ago, near to when I first made my Steam account. I don't remember thinking it was that fun, so I closed it, uninstalled it, and went on with my life.

I came back to it recently, and Jesus Christ does it have me hooked. I have space bases, storage places, tether lines stretching entire moons, tons of rocket ships, way more scrap metal than I would ever feasibly need, and giant tunnel systems going down to the core of planets. No day feels complete anymore without a dose of Astroneer in it.

If you have some money to give and some time to spare, I'd give this game a shot. Trust me, you'll thank me later.

Update: It turns out I'm lazy, and it turns out I don't have enough scrap. You live, you learn, I guess.

Great game, fun to play and explore different planets and build stuff. You can progress pretty quickly and the game is really basic. That is also its downfall, small planets and quick progression make for an easy game and I like a challenge and a game that will last longer. Not enough content for an exploration game. Gets a little lonely playing singleplayer, might be more fun if there was an online multiplayer option (not coop). Other than that, I would recommend this to anyone looking to kill a bit of time if you have some cash on the side or have a kid who would like to play a fun game.

System Era is using behavioral psychology to pressure players into purchasing from the in-game item shop in a PAID CO-OP title:

Shop—not settings—is the first tab in the menu

Items in the shop can't be earned through gameplay

Middle currency obfuscates the real dollar amounts players are spending

Prices ensure some currency is left over, encouraging additional purchases

Sound is used as positive reinforcement when buying an item, creating a sense of reward

Limited time discounts and rotational stock cause urgency to buy

Premium items are more distinctive designs, leading to social pressure to have an exclusive item

Over 50 new items were added to the shop, but three new items were added for the event

Shop was introduced on stream months ago as "a bundle" to avoid controversy

good game, ashame they had to turn down this route

I remember buying this game way back in beta when I didn't have a pc good enough to run it and I've seen it grow over several years and might I say this game turned out amazing. They've added so much and always listened to the community. This game is a super chill minecraft like game where you are an astronaut on some planets and you harvest resources to build your base bigger. An endless sandbox if you will. I wouldn't say it's my favorite game, but it is a really enjoyable game to sit down a relax with.I can't say how fun it would be to play with friends, but it probably is. Definitely recommend.

Closing thoughts: Astroneer is for anyone who loves discovery or automation, and not for people who are looking for intense combat or want to build anything other than bases. The game does offer microtransactions for strictly cosmetics, though a nice collection of free outfits become unlocked through the game. Astroneer has great replayability as well, and a standard playthrough will run about 30-45 hours to unlock most but not all of the content.

Drilled all the way to the core while playing with a friend of mine, touched the core and my tractor went flying, stranding me at the core.
My friend never came to rescue me 10/10 would drill again

For my taste this is the closest thing to a perfect game. Exploration, engineering (lite) and a clean, simple and powerful UI (that almost isn't a UI at all) It's amazing. On top of that for this stage of the game over a year since it came out in 50 hours of playtime I've run into exactly 1 bug (weird geography issue that got me stuck and forced a respawn) If you enjoy exploration and unlocking progressively more difficult planets and slowly ratcheting up the difficulty in establishing a working habitat/base this will scratch that itch. On top of it all there is a cool substory that I won't go into that you unfold over time and through your exploration. Highly recommend you avoid guide videos and just immerse yourself in the game and figure stuff out on your own. It's really all part of the experience is figuring out how the new stuff you are able to produce will work together. I would give an unqualified recommendation to buy and play this game. Super fun!

Very fun game with a big emphasis on exploration and resources. A survival game that only has oxygen as its main survival component which is easily manageable and lets you have freedom to just play without too many constraints, like not having to focus on things like hunger, thirst, etc as well.

Landscapes are beautiful and gives a true untouched nature feel, until you decide to do some of your own terraforming.
You get to travel to different planets, observing the unique environment and the local wildlife. Each planet has different resources with some being unique and you build resource bases accordingly.

Gets more fun when unlocking new technologies and you can start to have some automation if you're creative (or bored).
There's a sense of achievement being at your main base, surrounded by silos all filled with different resources.

Having friends join the team helps with base building and resource gathering, but still lets you have adventures of your own.
Amazing open world game to play to unwind and relax. So many peaceful adventures and nooks to explore.

This is a very fun and relaxing game. The game mechanics are simple, just need to worry about oxygen to breath, which frees the player's time allowing us to relax and focus on exploring, gathering, building, questing, etc. The procedurally created worlds ensure no two play-thrus are the same. The only negative thing about the game, it's no longer being developed, which is a shame. Maybe the software title would consider open-sourcing the source code so the community could continue developing it?

I have to say, Astroneer is one of the best games I have ever played. It was and is my go-to relaxing automation game and its visual style is completely unmatched that I have played since launch. I love this game with all of my heart but at some point I do need to stop the glaze as this game has slightly devolved as its current DLCs and updates just aren't like they used to be. I hope that the next update will bring a lot more content to help revive this game! But overall, PLAY THIS GAME if you like automation, fun designs, resource collecting, space exploration, building, or just anything that a sandbox of this caliber can produce, I suggest buying this game.
Hours of fun, runs well on low-spec hardware, enthralling story and collectible chess pieces! maybe the real simulation was the astroneers we killed along the way.

tldr.text: Very Positive (91%): players most often praise the co-op and multiplayer, especially playing with friends.
The main complaint is bugs and crashes, the most common gripe in reviews.

details.text: Recent reviews complain about bugs and crashes far less than before, so the stability complaints have eased.
New players are far less positive than veterans: 54% of those with little playtime are positive, against 94% of long-time players.
